title.narrative: ROAF/REG/HARNESSING PROPERTY RIGHTS: BUILDING RESILIENCE OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT AND INFORMAL WOMEN AND YOUTH TRADERS IN THE GREATER BUSIA METRO.

description.narrative:
The Harnessing Property Rights: Building Resilience of Local Governments and Informal Women and Youth Traders in the Greater Busia Metro (GBM), 2025-2028 project is a transformative initiative designed to improve land tenure security and foster economic resilience for informal women and youth traders in the cross-border region of Busia, spanning Kenya and Uganda. This project addresses systemic challenges related to insecure property rights, limited economic opportunities, and governance inefficiencies. It aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly those targeting poverty eradication, gender equality, and sustainable urban development.
Informal traders, particularly women and youth, face significant barriers due to insecure tenure and inequitable access to economic resources, undermining their livelihoods and regional economic growth. The project seeks to create a stable economic environment by promoting investment, fostering innovation, and improving governance for cross-border trade and security. By addressing these barriers, the initiative aims to uplift marginalized groups and drive sustainable local economic development.
The project employs a multi-faceted approach: • Land Tenure Security and Property Rights: It focuses on clarifying and mapping land tenure systems and deploying a digital Land Information System (LIS) as an enabler, towards towards providing informal traders with secure property rights. This enhanced security will open pathways to improved economic opportunities and investments. • Economic Resilience: The project will establish an integrated spatial economic development framework to promote local economic growth through diversification, technological innovation, and the formalization of micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs). Strengthened land revenue systems will bolster local fiscal capacities. • Governance and Cross-Border Trade: It seeks to improve governance frameworks for cross-border trade by building capacity among decision-makers, harmonizing legal structures, and utilizing evidence-based decision-making supported by robust data systems. Inclusivity is a cornerstone of this initiative, with active engagement of women, youth, and marginalized groups in every stage of planning and implementation. Partnerships with local governments, UN agencies, and civil society organizations ensure collaborative and sustainable development practices.
Expected Accomplishments: 1. Improved Land Tenure Security: Secured property rights for informal women and youth traders, enhancing their resilience and enabling access to economic opportunities. 2. Integrated Economic Development Framework: A comprehensive framework to foster investment, entrepreneurship, and economic growth in the Greater Busia Metro. 3. Strengthened Governance Frameworks: Improved systems for cross-border trade and security, reducing conflicts and promoting regional integration. 4. Capacity Building: Enhanced capabilities of local government authorities and stakeholders, enabling more effective planning, management, and policy implementation. By addressing the root causes of insecurity and economic vulnerability, the project is poised to transform the Greater Busia Metro into a hub of sustainable growth and opportunity. It not only supports the resilience and empowerment of women and youth but also strengthens regional integration and contributes to the broader objectives of sustainable development across East Africa.
